sentences.text: The fossil consists of parts preserved together in a chalk nodule, representing a subadult individual.
The preserved fossil piece measures 263 mm in length.
Its teeth were relatively short and conical with an oval cross-section, arranged in at least eight sockets per jaw, creating undulating outer sides due to bulging sockets.
At the time of its redescription, Mythunga was the most completely known pterosaur from Australia, a continent with fewer than twenty known pterosaur fossils.
Estimates of its size vary, with a 2007 calculation placing the wingspan at 4.7 meters and a 2018 revision suggesting a range of 4 to 6 meters.
The holotype fossil, which is the specimen the species is based on, was found in April 1991 by Philip Gilmore in Queensland, Australia.
The species Mythunga camara was named and described by Ralph Molnar and R. A. Thulborn in 2007/2008.
The genus name Mythunga refers to the constellation Orion in the local Aboriginal language.
Mythunga was redescribed by Adele Pentland and Stephen Poropat in 2018 after further preparation of the specimen.
Mythunga is a close relative of the Australian pterosaur Ferrodraco.
Kellner et al. placed Mythunga within the family Anhangueridae in 2010.
A 2019 analysis by Pentland et al. recovered Mythunga as a member of the subfamily Ornithocheirinae, sister to Ferrodraco.
However, a 2020 study by Borja Holgado and Rodrigo Pêgas reclassified Mythunga within the family Anhangueridae, specifically in the subfamily Tropeognathinae.
Richards et al. erected the clade Mythungini in 2023, which includes Mythunga and other Australian tropeognathines.
The Paleobiology Database lists the parent group of Mythunga as Tropeognathinae and the family as Anhangueridae.
Mythunga is classified in the class Reptilia.
The type species of the genus Mythunga is Mythunga camara.
Mythunga lived during the late Early Cretaceous (Albian age) in Australia.
Mythunga lived during the Albian stage, from 106.3 to 100.5 million years ago.
In 2025, Pêgas suggested Mythunga should be considered a nomen dubium because no proposed diagnostic characters were unique to the genus.
